{{Elections in Kentucky}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Kentucky''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the six [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Kentucky]], one from each of the state's six [[Kentucky's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections will coincide with [[United States House of Representatives elections, 2022|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]] and various [[2022 United States elections#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]].
{{toclimit|2}}

{{see also|Kentucky's 1st congressional district}}
The 1st district takes in [[Western Kentucky]], including [[Paducah, Kentucky|Paducah]], [[Hopkinsville, Kentucky|Hopkinsville]], [[Murray, Kentucky|Murray]], and [[Henderson, Kentucky|Henderson]]. The incumbent is Republican [[James Comer (politician)|James Comer]], who was re-elected with 75.0% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT">{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Cheryl L.|title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 3, 2020|url=http://history.house.gov/Institution/Election-Statistics/Election-Statistics/|publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives]]|date=February 28, 2019}}</ref>

{{see also|Kentucky's 2nd congressional district}}
The 2nd district encompasses west-central Kentucky, taking in [[Bowling Green, Kentucky|Bowling Green]], [[Owensboro, Kentucky|Owensboro]], and [[Elizabethtown, Kentucky|Elizabethtown]]. The incumbent is Republican [[Brett Guthrie]], who was re-elected with 70.9% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>

{{see also|Kentucky's 3rd congressional district}}
The 3rd district encompasses nearly all of [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville Metro]], which, since the merger of 2003, is consolidated with [[Jefferson County, Kentucky|Jefferson County]], though other incorporated cities, such as [[Shively, Kentucky|Shively]] and [[St. Matthews, Kentucky|St. Matthews]], exist within the county. The incumbent is Democrat [[John Yarmuth]], who was re-elected with 62.7% of the vote in 2020.<ref name="HPVT"/>
